name: Detail callouts: lock-on frame, arrows and counter
when: The voice points out three details in one frozen shot (the workhorse of a "300 details" video). A zoom punch onto detail 1 where a corner frame locks on, then pans to an arrow on detail 2 and one on detail 3; a counter ticks up after each. The still fills the frame.
anchor: Each callout lands on its word: the frame on detail 1 (`at1`), arrow 2 (`at2`), arrow 3 (`at3`). The camera starts moving 0.5 s (punch) or 0.9 s (pans) before.

vars.theme: clean or vice: the video's theme
vars.shot: the frozen shot: a 1920x1080 still in the project's assets/ (e.g. assets/footage/wall_16.jpg)
vars.shot_blur: the same still, blurred and dimmed to 60 %, baked with ffmpeg (no tint): ffmpeg -i shot.jpg -vf "gblur=sigma=6:steps=3,colorchannelmixer=rr=0.6:gg=0.6:bb=0.6" -q:v 2 shot_blur.jpg
vars.count: the counter's number once detail 1 lands; it shows count-1 first and counts up by one per detail (3 digits)
vars.label1: first line of the counter's label (default details)
vars.label2: second line of the counter's label (default spotted)
vars.box_x: detail 1's frame, left edge in pixels of the 1920x1080 still (box_y top, box_w width, box_h height); the punch centres on it
vars.arrow2_x: arrow 2's tip in still pixels (arrow2_y); arrow2_angle is the way it points: 0 right, 90 down, 180 left
vars.look2_x: the still point the camera centres on for detail 2 (look2_y), zoom2 its zoom; the camera clamps so the still always covers the frame
vars.arrow3_x: arrow 3's tip (arrow3_y, arrow3_angle), same as arrow 2
vars.at1: seconds after the start: the frame locks on detail 1 (the punch starts 0.5 s before; at least 0.6)
vars.at2: seconds after the start: arrow 2 lands (the pan starts 0.9 s before); at least 1.4 s after at1
vars.at3: seconds after the start: arrow 3 lands (the pan starts 0.93 s before); at least 1.4 s after at2
vars.out: seconds after the start: arrow 3 leaves; the scene can end 0.1 s later, or hold the shot up to 0.3 s more as validated

changed: The shot and its blurred copy are file values; the counter's digits are built from `count` (a digit that doesn't change stays still). The ground behind the still is gone: the still always covers the frame.
